findings.reason: §21 makes a closed day segment of a *running* job pass the retention scan's job check (line 849), so liveness is the only guard protecting exactly those files, and a node-scoped liveness read would delete them; the plan must name the retained query as the account-wide one, bounded through `node_probe.run_capture` (node_probe.py:186), whose argv it can bound without changing scope.
findings.text: §22 says the liveness read is routed "through that owner" (node_probe) and "the second query" deleted, but node_probe's job reader answers a different question from the one retention needs: `node_probe.read_jobs` (node_probe.py:696) issues `squeue -h -w <nodename> -o …`, scoped to one node, while `telemetry_retention.default_running_job_ids` (telemetry_retention.py:112) issues `squeue -h -o %i -u $USER`, scoped to the whole account; the plan does not say which survives, and the reading that deletes the account-wide query silently narrows liveness to the ingest node — the ingest loop runs on the CPU fleet node under the `ingest-cadence` decision (line 877), so a serve still running on a GPU node reads as ended

findings.reason: the reclaimable-space rationale rests on the 9.8 GB index, which I measured, and the schedule plus the vacuum are unchanged by the missing 534 MB artefact; the citation should be dropped or corrected to the scripts actually there, so a later reader is not sent looking for it.
findings.text: §22's "What is wrong, measured" names "A stale 534 MB `measure.sqlite3` from 2026-09-23" as sitting beside the index, and no such file exists in that directory: `ls -la ~/.cache/ambix/` shows `watch-index.sqlite3` (9,816,702,976 B) beside `build_index.py`, `cold_build.sh`, `measure_ingest.py` and `measure_skip.py`, the last two dated 2026-09-23, and a bounded search of `~/.cache`, `~/.local`, `~/.config` (depth 4) and `$HOME` (depth 3) finds no `measure.sqlite3` anywhere

findings.reason: if the disagreement proves to be a real defect in the tier-equality check, the node's retention gate can be red for a reason that says nothing about scheduled retention, and the two have to be closed on separate verdicts; the explanation belongs in its own node, or the file should wait outside this node's done-when.
findings.text: node `srw-scheduled-retention` (line 860) must deliver the scheduled retire-with-digest-recheck *and* produce "a recorded cause" for the unexplained 1278105 tier disagreement, which §22 itself says is not yet understood (line 853); the second is an investigation whose answer is unknown at dispatch

findings.reason: the site table is on disk in the normal case and the ordering is an implementation detail the node can settle (match against the pre-existing table, then refresh naming the slug); worth one line in §18 only if it is not obvious to the implementer.
findings.text: (LOW) §18's done-when requires the live `agent watch --json` render to append an `endpoints` row for the slug, but §17 appends an endpoints row only for a slug the refresh is given, and the slug is what `match_price` resolves from the table that same refresh produces (watch.py:317, :351): on a first run with no table, the render can name no slug, so the appended row this done-when asserts is not guaranteed
